paras: Hemiphyllodactylus harterti, also known commonly as the Bintang slender gecko, Hartert's slender gecko, and Werner's gypsy gecko, is a species  of lizard in the family Gekkonidae. The species is endemic to Peninsular Malaysia.
The specific name, harterti, is in honor of German ornithologist Ernst Johann Otto Hartert.
The preferred natural habitat of H. harterti is forest, at altitudes as high as 1,100 m (3,600 ft).

Adults of H. harteri have a snout-to-vent length (SVL) of about 4 cm (1.6 in), and a tail length slightly shorter than SVL. Males have 44–45 femoroprecloacal pores and a single cloacal spur (postanal tubercle).
H. harterti is nocturnal and scansorial (adapted for climbing).
Unlike other species of Hemiphyllodactylus which are unisexual (females only), H. harterti is bisexual (males and females).
